:::{#thm-kolmogorov-entropy}
#### Expected Kolmogorov complexity per symbol approaches the entropy

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be independent copies of a random variable $X$
that takes values in a finite set $\mathcal{X}$,
each value written as a fixed-length binary string,
and let $H_2(X)$ be the
[entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
of $X$ with base-2 logarithms.
Write $X^n = (X_1, \ldots, X_n)$.
There is a constant $c$ such that, for every $n \ge 1$,

$$
H_2(X)
\le \frac{1}{n} \Ep\left[K(X^n \mid n)\right]
\le H_2(X) + \frac{(\abs{\mathcal{X}} - 1) \log_2 n}{n} + \frac{c}{n}.
$$

So $\frac{1}{n} \Ep[K(X^n \mid n)] \to H_2(X)$ as $n \to \infty$.
This is Theorem 14.3.1 of @cover2006elements.

:::

::: {.proof}
For the lower bound, send each outcome $x^n$ of $X^n$
to a shortest program that outputs it given $n$.
Different outcomes get different programs, because a program determines its output,
and no halting program is a prefix of another,
so this is a prefix code for $X^n$, which makes it
[uniquely decodable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/source-coding.html#def-uniquely-decodable).
Its [expected length](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/source-coding.html#def-expected-length)
is $\Ep[K(X^n \mid n)]$.
If $X$ takes only one value with positive probability,
then $H_2(X) = 0$ and the lower bound holds trivially.
Otherwise, $X^n$ also takes at least two values with positive probability,
and part 1 of the
[source coding theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/source-coding.html#thm-source-coding)
gives $\Ep[K(X^n \mid n)] \ge H_2(X^n)$.
Applying the
[chain rule for entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#thm-entropy-chain-rule)
$n - 1$ times, and using that conditioning on independent variables
does not change entropy, gives $H_2(X^n) = n H_2(X)$.
Dividing by $n$ gives the lower bound.

For the upper bound, @cover2006elements [section 14.3] describe $x^n$ in two parts:
first how many times each value in $\mathcal{X}$ occurs,
which takes about $(\abs{\mathcal{X}} - 1) \log_2 n$ digits,
then which of the strings with those counts $x^n$ is,
which takes about $n H_2(X)$ digits on average.

:::
